content: A T-shaped uterus is a structural abnormality of the endometrial cavity that is most commonly associated with in utero exposure to diethylstilbestrol (DES). This abnormality is observed in approximately 31% of women who were exposed to DES during fetal development. Diethylstilbestrol (DES) is a synthetic estrogen that was first introduced in 1948. It was prescribed to pregnant women who experienced recurrent spontaneous abortions, premature deliveries, or other complications during pregnancy. The rationale behind its use was that DES could increase the synthesis of placental steroidal hormones, which was believed to reduce the likelihood of pregnancy loss. The diagnosis of a T-shaped uterus can be made using hysterosalpingography (HSG). On HSG imaging, the findings typically include a narrowed and irregular endocervical canal.
